neighbours.label: The opening of an aside that interrupts a clause mid-phrase: the ' (' or comma-phrase that starts a parenthetical such as '(to us)', '(issued in 2015)' or ', after the war,', before the sentence resumes; the same content placed outside the clause stays quiet.
fire: My aunt's habit (endearing to some, maddening to others) of humming at dinner never changed.
We finally bought a used (but nearly new) car for the trip.
The widespread use, after the war, of penicillin cut deaths sharply.
Critics pointed to the company's statement (issued in 2015) that nothing had changed.
The old (to me, at least) building on the corner has been sold.
His plan (which nobody had actually read) was approved by the board.
The rapid spread, during the 1990s, of mobile phones changed daily life.
Her quiet (some said cold) manner made the interviews difficult.
quiet: My aunt kept humming at dinner, and the habit never changed.
We finally bought a used car for the trip to the coast.
Penicillin came into wide use after the war and cut deaths sharply.
Critics pointed to a statement the company issued in 2015.
The old building on the corner has been sold to a developer.
Nobody had read his plan, but the board approved it anyway.
Mobile phones spread rapidly in the 1990s and changed daily life.
Her quiet manner made the interviews difficult for the reporters.

short: start of a mid-clause parenthetical aside
notes: Card: peaks on ' (' x10 and commas that open an interruption (habit (undoubtedly annoying...) of; adoption, after 1900, of; new (to us) house). Exploratory probe: asides 0.47-0.95, same sentences without the aside 0.004-0.07.
